source_text: Περὶ Καίσαρος καὶ Θεοῦ. Οἱ Φαρισαῖοι μετὰ τῶν Ἡρῳδιανῶν πειράζουσιν περὶ τοῦ κήνσου. Ὁ δὲ δείξας τὸ νόμισμα φησίν· «Ἀπόδοτε τὰ Καίσαρος Καίσαρι καὶ τὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ τῷ Θεῷ.» Ὅταν ὑπὸ τῶν ζητούντων ἀφορμὰς πειραζώμεθα, οὐ δεῖ παντελῶς σιγᾶν οὐδὲ εἰκῇ λαλεῖν, ἀλλὰ μετὰ εὐλαβείας ἀποκρίνεσθαι, ἵνα πᾶσαν ἀφορμὴν ἐκκόψωμεν καὶ τὰ πρὸς σωτηρίαν αὐτοῖς περιποιήσωμεν.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning Caesar and God. The Pharisees with the Herodians test about the census. But he having-shown the coin says: «Give-back the things of Caesar to Caesar and the things of God to God.» When by those seeking occasions we-are-tested, it-is-not-necessary wholly to-be-silent nor rashly to-speak, but with reverence to-answer, in-order-that every occasion we-may-cut-off and the things toward salvation for-them we-may-procure.
pass_b_english: On Caesar and God. Pharisees with Herodians test him about the census. Showing the coin he says: [[render to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s >> Bible:Matthew 22:21]]. When tested by those hunting occasions, we must neither go wholly silent nor speak rashly, but answer carefully so as to cut off every handle and secure what leads to salvation.
notes: Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
